Feature: Tenant creation, activation, and own-membership lookup
ExpectedBehavior: The screen can create/activate tenants and show the signed-in subject's tenant memberships.
ActualBehavior: POST /api/platform/tenants accepts CreateTenantRequest(Code; Name); POST /api/platform/tenants/{tenantId}/activate activates a tenant; GET /api/platform/tenants/mine returns TenantId and Role for active memberships. A separate administrator-only tenant directory GET with search/status/page/pageSize is mapped as API-PLT-TNT-001-004.
Remarks: Own-membership and administrator directory paths are separate; the Desktop screen currently calls own-membership.

ExpectedBehavior: The UI input/output fields match the API DTOs.
ActualBehavior: CreateTenantRequest has Code:string and Name:string. Activation has no request DTO and returns 204. Mine returns an anonymous array with TenantId:Guid and Role:string. Administrator directory responses expose TenantDirectoryView fields Id, Code, Name, Status, CreatedAtUtc.
Remarks: The Desktop own-membership view does not treat directory-only fields as membership response fields.

ExpectedBehavior: Tenant list supports ID/code/name/status/date filtering and paging.
ActualBehavior: Administrator directory GET supports search, status, page, and pageSize; the own-membership GET has no query parameters and returns an unpaged array. ID/date filtering is not registered.
Remarks: The Desktop own-membership view does not emulate the administrator directory query.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Only permitted administrators can mutate tenant state and subjects see only their memberships.
ActualBehavior: Create/membership/activate require PlatformAdministrator. Mine requires TenantMember and uses sub. Application services are concrete scoped registrations; platform repositories and unit of work are scoped. Tenant list/detail is not available to audit.
Remarks: Tenant membership integration also verifies an authenticated subject without persisted membership is denied.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports organization create, list, detail, update, and state management.
ActualBehavior: POST create, GET tenant-scoped list/detail, and PUT update routes are registered. No separate status action exists; status is the UpdateDirectoryEntryRequest.Status field.
EvidenceSymbols: PlatformEndpoints.MapPost organizations; MapGet organizations; MapGet organization; MapPut organization; PlatformDirectoryService
Remarks: Create verifies tenant is active and organization code is unique within tenant; Desktop currently uses list/create.

ExpectedBehavior: Organization fields in the screen match actual contract.
ActualBehavior: CreateOrganizationRequest has Code:string and Name:string; create returns anonymous { Id } with HTTP 201. Directory list/detail returns OrganizationDirectoryView fields Id, TenantId, Code, Name, Status; update accepts UpdateDirectoryEntryRequest(Name; Status).
Remarks: Directory response fields are distinct from the create response.

ExpectedBehavior: Organizations can be searched/paged by tenant, id, code, name, and status.
ActualBehavior: Tenant-scoped list supports search, status, page, and pageSize. ID/date filtering is not registered; detail is a separate route.
Remarks: The Desktop list passes SearchText, page, and pageSize to the API.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Organization mutation is tenant-scoped and administrator-protected.
ActualBehavior: TenantMember group plus TenantRouteAuthorizationFilter, TenantMembershipAuthorizationFilter, and TenantAdministratorAuthorizationFilter protect the route. PlatformProvisioningService is scoped; repositories/unit of work are scoped. Service verifies active tenant.
Remarks: Tenant/organization scope mismatch is covered by PlatformProvisioningService tests.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports project create, list, detail, update, and state management.
ActualBehavior: POST create, GET tenant-scoped list/detail, and PUT update routes are registered. No separate status action exists; status is the UpdateDirectoryEntryRequest.Status field.
EvidenceSymbols: PlatformEndpoints.MapPost projects; MapGet projects; MapGet project; MapPut project; PlatformDirectoryService
Remarks: Create verifies active tenant, active organization, and organization tenant ownership; Desktop currently uses list/create.

ExpectedBehavior: Project input/output fields are defined by actual DTOs.
ActualBehavior: CreateProjectRequest has Code:string and Name:string; create returns anonymous { Id } with HTTP 201. Directory list/detail returns ProjectDirectoryView fields Id, TenantId, OrganizationId, Code, Name, Status; update accepts UpdateDirectoryEntryRequest(Name; Status).
Remarks: TenantId and OrganizationId are route/filter values, not request-body fields.

ExpectedBehavior: Projects can be searched/paged by tenant, organization, id, code, name, and status.
ActualBehavior: Tenant-scoped list supports organizationId, search, status, page, and pageSize. ID/date filtering is not registered; detail is a separate route.
Remarks: The Client contract carries organizationId; Desktop list currently exposes search/page fields and command target organization ID.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Project mutation is organization- and tenant-scoped and administrator-protected.
ActualBehavior: Tenant route/membership/admin filters protect the route. PlatformProvisioningService is scoped and checks project organization/tenant/status before create.
Remarks: Cross-tenant organization rejection is covered by unit test.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports invite create, list/detail/status, expiry, resend, and cancel.
ActualBehavior: POST invitation create plus GET tenant-scoped user list/detail are registered. There is no separate invitation list/status/expiry/resend/cancel route; the list is a UserDirectoryView projection.
Remarks: The implementation is a user invite record, not a separate invitation aggregate/API.

ExpectedBehavior: Invitation input/output fields are actual API fields.
ActualBehavior: InviteUserRequest has Email:string and DisplayName:string. Response is anonymous { Id } with HTTP 201. No role/scope/expiry/status response is returned.
Remarks: The prior email/role/scope output list is not an API contract.

ExpectedBehavior: Invitations can be searched/paged by id, email, status, date, and requester.
ActualBehavior: User directory list supports search, status, page, and pageSize; invitation lifecycle fields such as requester/date/token are not registered.
Remarks: No token lifecycle or invitation-specific search can be wired.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Only a tenant administrator can create invitations within an active tenant.
ActualBehavior: Tenant route/membership/admin filters protect the route; PlatformProvisioningService is scoped and validates active tenant and tenant-scoped email uniqueness. No invitation token is exposed by the endpoint.
Remarks: Email uniqueness is tested tenant-scoped; no separate invitation security test exists.

Feature: Tenant, organization, and project membership grants
ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports membership grant, list, role change, revoke, and own-membership views.
ActualBehavior: Tenant/org/project grant routes, own memberships, and tenant/org/project membership list routes exist. No role-change or revoke route exists; Desktop currently uses tenant list/grant.
EvidenceSymbols: GrantAsync; GetMyMembershipsAsync; GrantOrganizationAsync; GrantProjectAsync; PlatformDirectoryService membership methods
Remarks: List routes are tenant-scoped and grant routes retain their scope-specific request DTOs.

ExpectedBehavior: Membership screen fields match actual request/response contracts.
ActualBehavior: GrantTenantMembershipRequest, GrantOrganizationMembershipRequest, and GrantProjectMembershipRequest each have SubjectId:string and Role:string. Grant responses are anonymous { Id }; mine response is an array of TenantId:Guid and Role:string. No membership status/granted-by/timestamp DTO is exposed.
Remarks: Role parsing uses TenantRole, OrganizationRole, or ProjectRole at the endpoint.

ExpectedBehavior: Memberships support scope, subject, role, status filtering and paging.
ActualBehavior: Tenant/org/project membership lists are registered but currently return unpaged scope-specific arrays; own-membership GET remains unpaged. No query filter parameters are registered.
EvidenceSymbols: MapGet membership routes; PlatformDirectoryService membership methods
Remarks: No client-side substitute should be treated as API filtering or paging.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Membership grants cannot cross tenant/org/project boundaries.
ActualBehavior: Tenant grant is PlatformAdministrator-only. Scoped grants require TenantMember plus tenant route/membership/admin filters, and ScopedMembershipService verifies target subject tenant membership and parent ownership/status. Services and repositories are scoped.
Remarks: Tenant membership persistence is exercised by ApiHost integration tests.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports policy list/create/detail/update/enable and an evaluation action.
ActualBehavior: GET/POST/PUT/PATCH policy routes exist. The policy evaluation service exists, but no evaluation API is registered; it is called by ScopedResourceAuthorizationFilter for resource/policy creation.
Remarks: No delete route either; existing PUT/PATCH changes record policy audit.

ExpectedBehavior: Policy list/editor fields match real contracts.
ActualBehavior: Create request fields OrganizationId:Guid?; ProjectId:Guid?; SubjectId:string; Action:string; ResourceType:string; Effect:string; Priority:int. Update fields Effect:string; Priority:int. Enable fields IsEnabled:bool. Create/list responses expose anonymous policy fields; update/enable return 204.
Remarks: Effect parses AuthorizationPolicyEffect; list has no dedicated response type.

ExpectedBehavior: Policy list supports scope, subject, action, resource, effect, enabled, priority filters and paging.
ActualBehavior: GET policy list accepts no query parameters and returns an unpaged tenant collection.
Remarks: Policy filtering is a separate API gap from evaluation.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Only tenant administrators can manage policies and policy scope must belong to selected tenant.
ActualBehavior: Tenant route/membership/admin filters protect all policy management routes. AuthorizationPolicyService is scoped; it verifies tenant/org/project status and ownership. PlatformAuthorizationService enforces explicit deny/allow semantics when used by scoped resource filters.
Remarks: Unit tests cover tenant membership, scoped access, explicit deny, and explicit allow.

Feature: Audit query, integrity, archive, schedule, job, retention
ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports audit search, integrity, archive, retry/verify, schedule, and retention operations.
ActualBehavior: All listed operation families have routes: paged audit query; integrity calculate/verify; archive create/verify; schedule get/update; archive-job create/get/retry/verify; retention get/update. No general archive list/export route exists.
EvidenceSymbols: AuthorizationAuditQueryService; AuthorizationAuditIntegrityService; AuthorizationAuditArchiveService; AuthorizationAuditArchiveScheduleService; AuthorizationAuditArchiveJobService; AuthorizationAuditRetentionService
Remarks: Archive operations are tenant scoped and bounded to 31-day windows/100,000 records where applicable.

ExpectedBehavior: Audit UI fields match actual query/request/result contracts.
ActualBehavior: Audit query params are subjectId?; action?; isAllowed?; fromUtc?; toUtc?; page=1; pageSize=50. Integrity request fields FromUtc; ToUtc; ExpectedSha256. Archive request fields FromUtc; ToUtc. Retention request fields RetentionDays; IsLegalHold; LegalHoldReason?. Response types and fields are recorded per endpoint in mapping.csv.
Remarks: No invented Auditor role is granted by the endpoint code.

ExpectedBehavior: Audit records support subject/action/allow/time filters and paging.
ActualBehavior: GET authorization-audit supports subjectId, action, isAllowed, fromUtc, toUtc, page, pageSize; pageSize is constrained 1-100. Integrity/archive operations use bounded UTC windows, not list paging.
Remarks: Audit query validation includes page/pageSize, time order, subject length, and action length.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Audit data and operational controls are tenant-admin only and preserve audit integrity.
ActualBehavior: All audit groups require TenantMember plus route/membership filters and TenantAdministrator filter. Audit application services are scoped; archive store is singleton; archive jobs/schedule use tenant-scoped repositories and leases. Actor values come from sub for mutating operations.
Remarks: Unit tests cover cross-tenant archive verification, retention, integrity, archive job retry, and failure cases.

Feature: Quota policy CRUD, history, and paging
ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports policy list/create/update/enable and history.
ActualBehavior: GET policy page, GET history, POST create, PUT update, and PATCH enabled are all registered. Each page uses total count/page/page size/items.
Remarks: Optimistic concurrency and change-audit behavior are implemented.

ExpectedBehavior: Quota editor fields match actual request/response records.
ActualBehavior: Create fields Scope; TargetId; TenantLimitBytes?; OrganizationLimitBytes?; ProjectLimitBytes?; DataSetLimitBytes?; WarningThresholdPercent=80; PlanCode?='Community'. Update fields ExpectedVersion; four nullable limits; WarningThresholdPercent; PlanCode. Enabled fields IsEnabled; ExpectedVersion. Response includes policy identity, scope/target, limits, warning threshold, plan, enabled, version, actor, timestamp; history includes before/after JSON.
Remarks: Actual policy TargetId is validated against tenant/org/project/dataSet ownership.

ExpectedBehavior: Quota policies support scope/target/plan search and paging.
ActualBehavior: Paging exists via page/pageSize; no scope, target, or plan-code filter query exists. Ordering is Scope then TargetId.
Remarks: The existing API supports paging but not the design's filter fields.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, tenant boundary, and concurrency
ExpectedBehavior: Tenant administrators manage only policies whose target is within the selected tenant.
ActualBehavior: Tenant route/membership/admin filters protect all routes. StorageQuotaPolicyManagementService is scoped and uses PlatformDbContext/DataSetDbContext; AddScoped registration is in ApiHost Program. Target validation, transactions, audit rows, and ExpectedVersion conflict handling are implemented.
Remarks: Integration test covers paging, auditing, optimistic concurrency, and quota threshold events.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports dataset create, list/search, detail, activation, archive, and restore.
ActualBehavior: POST create, GET tenant-scoped detail, and POST activate exist. No dataset list/search, rename/update, archive, restore, or delete route exists.
Remarks: Schema revisions are included in GET detail; activation requires a schema.

ExpectedBehavior: Dataset input/output fields match actual contracts.
ActualBehavior: CreateDataSetRequest fields OrganizationId:Guid; ProjectId:Guid; Name:string; StorageAdapter:string='sqlite'; ContentFormat:string='json-array'. The two scope IDs are non-nullable, contrary to the prior optional design fields. Detail returns Id; TenantId; OrganizationId; ProjectId; Name; StorageAdapter; ContentFormat; Status; Version; CreatedAtUtc; CurrentSchemaVersion; SchemaRevisions[Version; SchemaJson; CreatedAtUtc].
Remarks: Actual DTO contract is authoritative for UI input validation.

ExpectedBehavior: Dataset list supports ID/org/project/name/adapter/format/status search and paging.
ActualBehavior: No dataset list or query endpoint exists; detail is by required dataSetId route only.
Remarks: The screen cannot render a server-backed dataset list from current API.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Dataset data is isolated by tenant and mutation requires admin.
ActualBehavior: Dataset group requires TenantMember, route/header equality, active membership; create/activate add TenantAdministrator. DataSetManagementService is scoped; repository, scope validator, adapter resolver, and quota contracts are registered through DataSet DI/ApiHost. Repository reads take tenantId.
Remarks: Integration tests prove cross-tenant detail/content access is rejected.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports schema register/current version/revision history and dedicated revision search/detail.
ActualBehavior: POST schemas appends an immutable revision and GET dataset detail exposes CurrentSchemaVersion and SchemaRevisions. No dedicated revision search/detail/diff/rollback route exists.
Remarks: The shared dataset detail endpoint is mapped explicitly in mapping.csv.

ExpectedBehavior: Schema fields match actual request and response.
ActualBehavior: AddDataSetSchemaRequest has SchemaJson:string. Response is anonymous { DataSetId:Guid; SchemaVersion:int } with HTTP 201. Dataset detail returns each revision's Version:int; SchemaJson:string; CreatedAtUtc:DateTimeOffset.
Remarks: No ExpectedDataSetVersion field exists on the actual schema registration request.

ExpectedBehavior: Schema revisions support DataSet/version/date search and paging.
ActualBehavior: No revision query parameters or paged revision route exists; revisions are embedded in dataset detail.
Remarks: UI must use the full dataset detail response or wait for API addition.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Schema writes are admin-only and cannot cross tenant dataset ownership.
ActualBehavior: Schema POST inherits TenantMember/route/membership filters and adds TenantAdministrator. DataSetManagementService.GetAsync/AddSchemaAsync pass tenantId to repository; service is scoped.
Remarks: Tenant-scoped schema/activation behavior is covered by application and integration tests.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports upload/download, dataset usage, tenant usage/history, quota events, and file/version/delete/recovery operations.
ActualBehavior: Upload, download, dataset usage, tenant usage, usage history, and quota-event history routes exist. File listing, content versioning, delete, restore, and dedicated download metadata routes do not exist.
Remarks: Storage references remain opaque and content is streamed.

ExpectedBehavior: Storage screen fields match actual body/response contracts.
ActualBehavior: Upload uses HttpRequest.Body with no DTO and returns 204; download returns application/octet-stream Stream; dataset usage returns TenantBytes/TenantDataSetCount/OrganizationBytes/OrganizationDataSetCount/ProjectBytes/ProjectDataSetCount/DataSetBytes/Limits/UtilizationPercent/WarningThresholdPercent/Warnings/MeasuredAtUtc; tenant usage returns TenantBytes/TenantDataSetCount/MeasuredAtUtc; history/events return arrays with fields listed in mapping.csv.
Remarks: No raw storage reference or internal path is returned.

ExpectedBehavior: Storage content and usage support DataSet/type/format/date/event filters and paging.
ActualBehavior: Only history/quota-event endpoints accept take; content and usage endpoints have no filters; take has defaults and range validation but no date/event-type filters.
Remarks: No list/search API should be inferred from usage aggregates.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, and tenant boundary
ExpectedBehavior: Content and usage are tenant-scoped; writes/events are admin-protected where required.
ActualBehavior: All routes use TenantMember plus route/membership filters; content write and quota events add TenantAdministrator. Adapter/usage reader are singleton; platform quota provider is registered scoped in Program; DataSetManagementService and snapshot service are scoped. Storage adapter tests verify tenant isolation and atomic quota.
Remarks: Integration and infrastructure tests cover cross-tenant content/usage and quota transitions.

Feature: Profile, revision, execution, result, detail, and deletion flows
ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports profile CRUD/list, execution scheduling/list/detail, results, detail paging, and deletion.
ActualBehavior: Profile create/revision create, execution create, execution result GET, detail GET, and execution DELETE exist. Profile list/detail and execution list/search are not registered.
EvidenceSymbols: CreateProfileAsync; AddProfileRevisionAsync; CreateExecutionWithStatusAsync; GetExecutionAsync; GetDetailsAsync; DeleteExecutionAsync
Remarks: Execution scheduling also enqueues Worker task dataset.validation.v1 and compensates on enqueue conflict/unavailable.

ExpectedBehavior: Validation profile/execution/detail fields match actual contracts.
ActualBehavior: Profile create fields Name; DefinitionJson. Revision field DefinitionJson. Execution fields ExpectedDataSetVersion:int; SchemaVersion:int; ProfileId:Guid; ProfileRevision:int plus Idempotency-Key header. Execution response includes FencingToken and DetailReference as well as counters/status/failure/timestamps. Detail items are RowNumber; FieldName?; Code; Severity; Message.
Remarks: The API does not return raw cell values; messages/details are bounded by validation implementation.

ExpectedBehavior: Profiles/executions support DataSet/profile/execution/status/date/failure filters and paging.
ActualBehavior: Only validation details support skip/take (defaults 0/100); result/profile/execution collection routes and filters are absent.
Remarks: Detail page bounds are validated; collection navigation is an API gap.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, tenant boundary, idempotency
ExpectedBehavior: Validation data is tenant-scoped; admin controls mutation and execution scheduling.
ActualBehavior: Result/detail GET require TenantMember plus route/membership. Profile/revision/create/delete require TenantAdministrator. DataSetValidationService and WorkerTaskEnqueueService are scoped. Create execution validates active dataset, expected version, schema/profile revisions, and Idempotency-Key; Worker enqueue conflict is compensated.
Remarks: Integration tests cover idempotent execution and tenant boundary; application tests cover profile parsing and engine behavior.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports task register/list/detail/status/progress/cancel/retry/result.
ActualBehavior: POST task registration and GET task detail/status exist. Status includes progress and HasResult. No task list/search, cancel, force retry, or result download endpoint exists.
Remarks: Task payload/reference bodies are intentionally not returned.

ExpectedBehavior: Task monitor fields match actual body/header/result contracts.
ActualBehavior: Enqueue body fields TaskType; PayloadReference; MaxAttempts=5 and required Idempotency-Key header. Create response exposes Id; TaskType; Status; CreatedAtUtc. Status GET exposes Id; TaskType; Status; AttemptCount; MaxAttempts; FencingToken; CheckpointVersion; CreatedAtUtc; NextAttemptAtUtc; CompletedAtUtc; LastErrorCode; LeaseExpiresAtUtc; ProgressPercent; ProgressStage; ProgressMessage; HasResult.
Remarks: No DTO for task result body is exposed.

ExpectedBehavior: Task list supports task id/type/status/date/error filters and paging.
ActualBehavior: No task collection route or query parameters exist; only taskId detail lookup is available.
Remarks: Worker repository has internal queue pagination, but that is not a public screen API.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, tenant boundary, idempotency
ExpectedBehavior: Only tenant administrators can register/inspect tasks and key reuse is tenant-safe.
ActualBehavior: Routes require TenantMember, route/header match, active membership, and TenantAdministrator. Enqueue/query services are scoped; Worker repository/DbContext are scoped. Idempotency-Key is required/max 200 and task type must be enabled.
Remarks: Worker repository tests cover tenant queues, fencing, and persistence boundaries.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports DLQ list/detail, failure filters, replay, and replay history.
ActualBehavior: GET dead-letters is paged and POST replay creates/reuses replay work. There is no task-detail endpoint under DLQ, failure filter query, replay history/specific reason API.
Remarks: Original task is preserved by repository behavior; replay header is idempotency boundary.

ExpectedBehavior: DLQ fields and replay inputs match actual contract.
ActualBehavior: List query uses page:int=1 and pageSize:int=50; item fields Id; TaskType; Status; AttemptCount; MaxAttempts; LastErrorCode; CreatedAtUtc; NextAttemptAtUtc. Replay has no body and requires Replay-Request-Id:GUID header; response OriginalTaskId; ReplayTaskId.
Remarks: No replay reason or attempt history fields are returned.

ExpectedBehavior: DLQ supports TaskId/type/status/error/date filters and paging.
ActualBehavior: Paging exists with page/pageSize and bounds 1-100; no other filter query parameters exist.
Remarks: Invalid page overflow and range are handled as 400.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, tenant boundary, replay idempotency
ExpectedBehavior: DLQ access and replay are tenant-admin only and cannot cross tenant/task state boundaries.
ActualBehavior: Route/membership/admin filters protect both operations. WorkerTaskDeadLetterService is scoped and repository is scoped. Replay validates tenant/task IDs, non-empty GUID, requestedBy sub, and passes Replay-Request-Id to tenant-scoped repository.
Remarks: Integration and infrastructure tests cover admin requirement, cross-tenant/non-DLQ rejection, and original preservation.

ExpectedBehavior: The screen supports delivery create/list/detail/status/retry.
ActualBehavior: POST delivery create returns 202 with delivery projection and WorkerTaskId; GET detail returns delivery state. No list/search or dedicated retry route exists; worker handler retries transient failures automatically.
Remarks: Screen should expose only the safe projection; payload is not returned.

ExpectedBehavior: Delivery fields match actual request/response contracts.
ActualBehavior: CreateExternalDeliveryRequest fields TargetUri:string; Payload:JsonElement; MaxAttempts=5 plus required Idempotency-Key. Create response contains Delivery projection Id; TenantId; TargetUri; IdempotencyKey; Status; AttemptCount; MaxAttempts; LastErrorCode; CreatedAtUtc; CompletedAtUtc, plus WorkerTaskId and Created. Detail returns same projection. Payload is omitted.
Remarks: Actual API does not return Payload even though it is stored for Worker execution.

ExpectedBehavior: Delivery monitor supports id/URI/status/error/date search and paging.
ActualBehavior: No collection endpoint or query parameters exist; only deliveryId detail is public.
Remarks: Automatic Worker retry state exists but is not directly commandable from API.

Feature: Authorization, service, DI, tenant boundary, idempotency, target policy
ExpectedBehavior: Delivery creation is admin-only, detail is member-readable, target URI is allow-listed, and same-key reuse is tenant-safe.
ActualBehavior: Create requires TenantMember plus route/membership/admin; detail requires TenantMember plus route/membership. ExternalDeliveryService is typed HttpClient; repository scoped; ExternalDeliveryOptions singleton. Target must be absolute HTTP/HTTPS without user info and in allowed hosts or development loopback; same-key different payload/target/max attempts conflicts.
Remarks: Integration/infrastructure tests cover idempotency, response loss, 5xx/timeout, cancellation, target loopback policy, and tenant isolation.
